**Proof idea.** For a rational `x = p/q` in lowest terms, `x - 1/x = (p² − q²)/(pq)` is also in lowest terms. With height `H(x) = |num| + den`, this gives `H(f x) ≥ H(x) + 1` for every `x ∈ S`. Iterating, `H(f^[n] z) ≥ n` for any `z ∈ S`. If `y` were in every `f^[n] '' univ`, taking `n = H(y) + 1` would force `H(y) ≥ H(y) + 1`, a contradiction. The `↔ True` side is then immediate.
